record_identity.title: Compromised Mistral SDK package executed credential-harvesting payload on import

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Mini Shai-Hulud / TanStack compromise affecting Mistral SDK releases
incident_identity.date_basis: Mistral states compromised npm packages were uploaded on 11 May 2026 and the compromised PyPI release on 12 May 2026; affected releases were removed within hours.

summary: Mistral reported that the Mini Shai-Hulud supply-chain attack on TanStack resulted in compromised Mistral npm and PyPI SDK versions being published. The compromised PyPI package `mistralai==2.4.6` executed malicious code on import, downloading a background payload that harvested credentials from common locations. Mistral reported no impact to its global infrastructure and removed the affected releases. Its updated advisory says the compromised npm releases referenced a missing file, preventing their malicious path from running. The working PyPI payload was Linux-specific. Mistral later marked mitigation and closed its investigation.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Mistral's security advisory identifies affected npm and PyPI versions, publication windows and indicators of compromise. It states that the compromised PyPI release executed a malicious script on Linux at import time and launched a detached process designed to harvest credentials. Aikido Security separately reports that its malware team detected compromised npm package versions including @mistralai releases in the wider campaign. Its account documents external post-publication detection, not the exact Mistral internal monitoring control or the causal route to removal. The updated advisory distinguishes nonfunctional npm payload paths from the working Linux PyPI import path. Investigation closure on 14 May does not prove downstream customer cleanup or absence of credential exposure.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Trusted package-distribution channels carried malicious code into an AI software development kit. The governance problem is therefore not a model output but the integrity of the software supply chain through which developers receive AI tooling, including package provenance, release controls and the authority of third-party maintainers. Aikido’s external detection and Mistral’s removal show a distinct post-publication response stage. The available accounts do not establish that a specific Mistral pre-publication control was required and failed, or that the external monitoring was the operative control that caused removal. Package identity substitution and the link between external detection and provider removal remain ambiguous. Import-time malware is distinct from GAI output; removal does not prove a prepublication control duty or global compromise. The AI software-distribution security outcome is Not aligned. Withdrawal of the affected releases is Aligned with the repair requirement. Monitoring and security-review processes remain Boundary where their operative evidence is not available.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: AI-system governance includes the developer infrastructure surrounding a model. Compromised package provenance can expose credentials and downstream systems before the model is ever invoked, making third-party build dependencies, release integrity and incident response part of the assurance boundary.
assessment_boundaries: Mistral reports no impact to its global infrastructure.
The npm packages were compromised but Mistral reports their malicious code path was non-functional; the PyPI package did execute a credential-harvesting payload.
The public advisory does not quantify how many customers installed or executed the affected PyPI release or whether credentials were successfully exfiltrated from customer systems.

external_assessments.assessment_title: TanStack supply chain attack affecting Mistral SDK packages
external_assessments.scope_note: The security advisory diagnoses the same software-supply-chain occurrence but does not quantify customer execution or successful credential exfiltration.
external_assessments.assessment_summary: Mistral identifies compromised SDK releases, publication windows and a PyPI import-time payload that launched credential-harvesting code, while reporting no impact to Mistral's global infrastructure.
external_assessments.vigil_comparison_note: VIGIL treats the occurrence as a software-supply-chain package-provenance and release-integrity failure in ordinary-language governance terms, while retaining the Incident as unclassified under Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 because no current selectable class precisely encodes malicious package-distribution substitution.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: Mistral removed the affected SDK releases after publication. This repaired the distribution path for those versions.
